stimulus.body: 次の語について考えましょう：sora。

questions.stem: Which hiragana form is the kun-yomi of 空, the kanji for "sky"?

options.misconception: confuses the native reading of 空 with the kun-yomi of another character
confuses the native reading of 空 with the kun-yomi of another character
confuses the native reading of 空 with the kun-yomi of another character

questions.explanation: The kun-yomi of 空, meaning "sky", is sora. This native Japanese reading is typically used when the kanji appears alone or with okurigana, whereas the on-yomi kuu appears in many compound words.
questions.hint: Recall the Japanese reading sora used for 空 on its own.

questions.subject: JAPANESE
questions.learningObjective: identify the on-yomi of a kanji

stimulus.body: 次の語について考えましょう：ten。

questions.stem: What is the on-yomi reading of the kanji 天 meaning "heaven"?

options.misconception: gives the reading of a different kanji rather than the on-yomi of 天
gives the reading of a different kanji rather than the on-yomi of 天
gives the reading of a different kanji rather than the on-yomi of 天

questions.explanation: The kanji 天, meaning "heaven", has the on-yomi ten. The on-yomi is the reading borrowed from Chinese and is common in compound words, while the kun-yomi is the native Japanese reading used when the character stands alone.
questions.hint: Recall the Chinese-derived reading borrowed for the kanji 天.
